URL: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/may/19/andy-burnham-confirmed-as-labour-candidate-for-makerfield-byelection
TITLE: Andy Burnham confirmed as Labour candidate for Makerfield byelection
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-19 12:56 (updated 15:34)
AUTHORS: Jessica Elgot, Ben Quinn
SOURCE: The Guardian

KEY:
- Burnham confirmed by Labour's NEC as Makerfield candidate today
- No other candidates shortlisted by Labour (NEC sources: others applied but not shortlisted)
- By-election expected 18 June (date pending Commons confirmation)
- Reform UK announced candidate Robert Kenyon — local plumber, army reservist, ex-NHS specialist technician, came within 5,399 votes of Simons in 2024

BURNHAM QUOTES:
- "Humbled" to have been selected
- Places of Makerfield "neglected by national politics for too long"
- "These proud working-class communities represent the very best values of our country and they deserve so much better"
- "Many people here feel Westminster isn't working for them and they are right. I am standing to change that and get the voice of these communities heard loud and clear"
- People needed life "to be more affordable again"
- This week: setting out economic agenda; ruling out any imminent EU return; recommitting to fiscal rules on borrowing/debt

FARAGE/REFORM:
- "David versus Goliath battle"
- "This is the 'The Plucky Plumber' taking on 'Open Borders Burnham.' Only Reform UK can beat Labour in this byelection"
- Kenyon video: Makerfield was a "stepping stone" for Burnham; "career politicians" attack on private school/Cambridge background

CONTEXT:
- Wigan borough: Burnham won 66% in 2024 mayoral; Labour lost 24/25 council seats to Reform in May 2026 locals
- Restore Britain (rightwing rival): Rebecca Shepherd
- Green candidate Wednesday; Conservative within 24 hours
- If elected, Burnham "expected to quickly move to challenge Keir Starmer for the Labour leadership"
